result:
I'd avoid stating causation in the title, since all we have is a timing correlation. If lag turns out not to be the cause, a "caused by consumer lag" title sends the investigation down the wrong path. You can still get it routed to the right squad by naming lag in the title as a suspected factor.

**Title:**
Nightly report missing ~1,200 orders on 2026-10-08, coincides with Kafka consumer lag spike (suspected cause)

**Description:**
The nightly order report was missing ~1,200 orders for the 2026-10-08 run, and the Kafka consumer lag dashboard shows a spike at about the same time; please confirm whether the lag caused the gap (for example, the report job ran before the consumer caught up) or whether something else dropped the orders.

Two details would make the ticket easier to act on:
- The exact time window of the lag spike and the consumer group or topic affected.
- The nightly job's start time, so the data team can check if it ran before the lag cleared.

A quick check that would confirm or rule out lag: see whether the 1,200 missing orders now appear in the warehouse (late arrival) or are absent entirely (dropped). If they arrived late, lag is very likely the cause and you can retitle the ticket accordingly. If they never arrived, the cause is probably elsewhere.

I'm assuming the date is yesterday relative to today (2026-10-09), so adjust it if the report covers a different day.
